subject: general
question: In which of the following years, Uttarakhand had received an unusual amount of rainfall, which led to the melting of the Chorabari glacier and the eruption of the Mandakini river?
solution:
The correct answer is **__2013__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2013**, the **state of Uttarakhand** saw unusually **heavy rain** from **June 13 to June 17.**
 
• As a result, the** Mandakini river **erupted and the **Chorabari glacier** began to melt.
 
• Large portions of **Western Nepal, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand** were also hit by the **floods.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One such glacier is India's **Chorabari Glacier**, which feeds important rivers like the **Ganges**.
 
• This **glacier**, which is located between the village of **Kedarnath** and the Kedarnath mountain to the north and south, creates a ferocious stream that finally joins the **Ganges River.**
 
• At** Rudraprayag**, the** river Mandakini**, which is the most significant river flowing from the Kedarnath peak's slopes, joins the **Alaknanda**.
 
• Actually, the **Chorabari Glacier**'s snowmelt feeds the river's springs, which are located around one mile above **Kedarnath Temple.**
